key_insight: Eu²⁺/Eu³⁺ redox chemistry pins the Fermi level, overcoming self-limiting nitrogen incorporation in titanate-derived perovskite oxynitrides.
engineering_relevance: Fermi-level engineering offers a synthesis strategy for tuning oxynitride composition, though the abstract reports neither AI methods nor solar-cell performance.
method: Combine theoretical modelling with experimental characterisation of titanate oxynitrides.
Use Eu/Ba and Eu/Ca A-site substitution to control charge compensation.
Relate nitrogen uptake to Fermi-level shifts and structural distortion.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports nitrogen incorporation limited to 0.03 per formula unit in barium titanate oxynitrides, versus up to 0.65 with Eu-enabled compensation measured by hot gas extraction, with Fermi-level pinning near 2.9 eV above the valence-band maximum.
watch_item: Further nitrogen incorporation remains limited by bond-angle distortion within Ti(O,N)₆ octahedra.
paper_title: Controlling nitrogen incorporation in (Eu,Ba,Ca)TiO$_3$-derived perovskite-type oxynitrides through Fermi Level Engineering
